newsitem.title: USA: Honda Accord takes top survey award.
newsitem.headline: Honda Accord takes top survey award.

text.p: Honda Motor Co's Accord beat out the Toyota Motor Corp Camry and Chevrolet Lumina for the top ranking among premium mid-size cars in J.D. Power and Associate's 1997 Initial Quality Study.

The closely watched annual survey, released Wednesday, also showed that Ford Motor Co 's F-Series took top honors in the full-size pickup truck category, followed by the Chevrolet C/K and Toyota T100 pickup trucks.
The overall industry average for cars and trucks combined for 1997 model-year vehicles dropped to 86 problems per 100 vehicles from 110 problems a year ago.
The 22 percent improvement is the largest since the inception of the study in 1987, said J.D. Power, an international research firm based in Agora Hills, Calif.
The study measures problems from 89 different areas reported by consumers in the first 90 days of ownership. The 1997 study includes responses from more than 43,000 owners.

J.D. Power refused to disclose how individual automakers fared. In separate press releases, General Motors Corp said it improved 18 percent from the 1996 model year study, while Chrysler Corp said it registered a 20 percent improvement.
Ford Motor Co said it improved 28 percent over a year ago, the best of Detroit's Big Three.

Large improvements in the quality of high-volume vehicles are behind the 1997 industry improvement, the research firm said. Overall, high-volume vehicles improved by 31 percent versus 23 percent for mid-volume vehicles, while vehicles produced in low volumes show only a 13 percent improvement.

"What we are now seeing is the ability of manufacturers to take what they have learned in producing high quality, low-volume vehicles and apply these concepts to the production of high-volume vehicles," said Chance Parker, director of product research.

The leaders of other individual car segments include: Saturn SL and Toyota Tercel tied for compact car; Nissan Altima for entry midsize car; Acura Integra for sporty car; Infiniti I30 for entry luxury car; and Lexus LS400 for premium luxury car.
On the truck side, Toyota TAcoma won for compact pickup; Honda Odyssey for compact van; Infiniti QX4 for compact sport/utility vehicle; and Lexus LX450 for full-size sport/utility.
